title: A library asset swap writes only the Space preference keys it rewrites

source.ref: Space function scan 2026-11-18, a whole-blob writer LIVE-2347's residual named (lib/library/usage.ts)

detail: The library's global asset swap (swapLibraryAssetRefs, asset A becomes asset B everywhere) read each listed Space's spaces.preferences, rewrote the refs with swapSpacePreferences and wrote the whole object back with .update({ preferences }) from the admin client. A swap landing beside a save from another console (a Spotlight publish, a website editor stub, a menu save) could undo it. Fixed: the swap diffs the rewritten bag against its read (lib/spaces/preferences-patch.ts preferencesPatch) and sends only the top-level keys it rewrote (pageDocs, the legacy puck doc, profileLayout, profileLayoutDraft) through the set_space_preferences RPC (SCAN-833) on the same admin client. The function is service_role only, which is the caller this path already uses (the Studio-gated action applies authz), so no signed-in owner is needed and nothing is weakened. One write per Space, the mid-way failure message, the idempotent retry and every other store are unchanged. No migration. Residual: the RPC merges top-level keys only, so a swap and a page save racing on the SAME key (pageDocs) can still overwrite each other inside that key, as for LIVE-2347.

verify.note: Fails while lib/library/usage.ts replaces the whole preferences blob instead of sending a key-scoped patch. Behavior test: lib/library/usage.test.ts (the LIVE-2352 block, including a key saved between the read and the write surviving the swap).
